prompts.EXPLAIN_BATCH_INSTRUCTION: For every test in tests, write 2-3 sentences for a test engineer: what the test checks, why it matters for the requirement, and the expected outcome. Answer with JSON {"explanations": [{"test_id": ..., "explanation": ...}]} containing exactly one entry per test, using the given test_id values. Plain prose only; do not write byte values.
prompts.PARSE_INSTRUCTION:
Extract the UDS identifiers in requirement_text, using only keys from spec_index. Work in this order and add nothing the text does not mention or clearly imply.
1. services: the service for the main action (never empty). read/report a value -> 0x22; write/set/change a value or calibration -> 0x2E; switch/enter/return to a session or mode -> 0x10; unlock/seed/key -> 0x27; ECU reset/reboot -> 0x11; keep-alive/tester present -> 0x3E; start/stop/results of a routine or self-test -> 0x31; read fault memory/trouble codes -> 0x19; clear them -> 0x14.
2. dids / routines: match the words of the text to the names in spec_index (a stored setting is a DID, something started or run is a routine). Only values the text names.
3. sessions: default -> 0x01, programming/flash -> 0x02, extended/diagnostic mode -> 0x03. Also add service 0x10 only if being in that session is a condition ('shall require extended mode', 'only in the flash session'); 'in any/every session' is not.
4. security: only if the text mentions unlock, security access, seed/key or a level: add service 0x27 and the level (level 1 -> 0x01, programming-level -> 0x03). Otherwise leave security_levels empty and do not add 0x27.
5. intents from allowed_intents, 2-4 keywords.
6. evidence: for each service, did, routine or dtc you list, copy a short phrase (2-6 words) exactly as written in requirement_text: {"service:<service id>": "<phrase>", "did:<id of X>": "<phrase>"}. Leave out items you cannot quote; an item whose phrase is not in the text is discarded.
Examples (made-up requirements; <id of X> stands for the key of the spec_index entry whose name matches X, never copy an identifier from an example):
'<X> shall be readable in every session.' -> services [0x22], dids [<id of X>], sessions [0x01,0x02,0x03]
'<Y> must give results only after it was started.' -> services [0x31], routines [<id of Y>]
'Changing <Z> shall need extended mode and a level 1 unlock.' -> services [0x10,0x27,0x2E], dids [<id of Z>], sessions [0x03], security_levels [0x01]
If the text names no matching entry for dids, routines or DTCs, leave that list empty.
prompts.PLAN_INSTRUCTION: Choose a small, focused set of test cases (usually 4-8) that verify this requirement. Only pick options about the requirement's own DID, routine or service; skip options about other identifiers. Cover each category the requirement needs, one or two options each: positive (the behaviour works), negative (wrong value, length, sub-function or order is rejected), session (the service is refused in the wrong session), security (locked access, lockout or relock, whenever an unlock or security level is involved), timing (only for session timeout or keep-alive). Each choice is a template_id and one of its option_index values from the list, with a one-sentence rationale that names the part of the requirement it checks. Do not repeat a choice.
prompts.SCHEMA_RETRY_INSTRUCTION:
Your previous reply was not valid JSON for the required schema. Error: {error}
Reply again with only a JSON object that matches the schema.
prompts.SYSTEM_PROMPT: You are a UDS (ISO 14229) diagnostics test-planning assistant for an automotive ECU. You never write request or response bytes. You only reference identifiers that exist in the provided spec index, choose template ids and option indices from the provided catalog, and write short plain-English prose. Answer with JSON matching the schema when one is required.
